note: Posture is cautious for two reasons that compound each other. First, two large market-moving data prints hit at 8:30 AM ET today — PCE inflation (the metric the Fed targets at 2%) and the Q2 GDP second estimate — creating meaningful intraday volatility risk before the market even settles. Second, Fed Chair Warsh speaks at Jackson Hole tomorrow, the single highest-profile annual Fed policy signal of the year; markets routinely move on his words, and we cannot know in advance whether the tone will be hawkish or dovish. A Friday NFP benchmark revision adds a third event this week. On top of the event calendar, the market is objectively expensive: trailing PE 26-29x is 35-60% above the historical median, CAPE is ~39x, and the 10-year yield at ~4.7% is restrictive. Our three thesis candidates (AAPL, MSFT, V) all trade 26-60% above our base fair value, so no actionable buy exists regardless of posture. Cautious does not mean sell; it means we demand a larger margin of safety before adding to any position, and we hold cash patiently through this high-event-density window.
